sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.provenance_note: Official author archive. Cover says October 2010, but the available file contains later updates. Reprinted forecast passages are used for attribution; the author’s favorable self-grades are not independent outcome evidence. Original book editions were not inspected. Page locators below are PRINTED pages, not PDF viewer indices.

sources.title: Spiritual Machines: The Merging of Man and Machine — Ray Kurzweil
sources.provenance_note: Attributed to Kurzweil; closing note identifies adaptation from The Age of Spiritual Machines (1999). An article mirror, not a scan of the book. Text transcription may contain errors. The article’s dollar amounts must not silently replace differently quoted book versions.

sources.title: Long Bets #1 — Kapor/Kurzweil Turing-test agreement
sources.provenance_note: Kapor takes the NO side; Kurzweil takes the opposing side. Detailed test conditions belong to this contract, not to every generic use of “Turing test.”

sources.title: So what is the singularity? — Ray Kurzweil Q&A
sources.provenance_note: Page identifies the dialogue as 2005. Store dialogue year 2005 separately from archive publication date 2011. Not a checked scan of the 2005 book.

sources.title: AI escape velocity: A conversation with Ray Kurzweil
sources.provenance_note: Bessemer hosts the interview and timestamped transcript. Do not attribute interviewer comments to Kurzweil. The Q&A section is explicitly summarized; cited passages below are in the main transcript.

sources.title: Ray Kurzweil: Universal basic income will arrive in the 2030s
sources.provenance_note: Secondary, contemporaneous attribution of a TED appearance. Original event transcript was not obtained; lower attribution confidence. Not used as technical outcome evidence.

sources.title: Solar power to rule in 20 years, futurists say
sources.provenance_note: Archived event reporting, not an original talk transcript. Review must distinguish solar from all renewables and energy from electricity.

sources.title: IBM — Deep Blue
sources.provenance_note: Documents the 1997 match victory; not proof of the original date or wording of Kurzweil’s forecast.

sources.title: Apple unveils new PowerBook
Apple introduces MacBook Air
Apple unveils one-inch-thick Titanium PowerBook G4
Introducing Amazon Kindle
iTunes Store tops over five billion songs sold
iPhone App Store downloads top 10 million
Apple introduces wireless keyboard and mouse
Wireless Internet Use — Pew Research Center
sources.provenance_note: US adult survey. Ever-used wireless access is not a majority-of-traffic measure and is not global coverage.

sources.title: Apple launches iPhone 4S, iOS 5 and iCloud
sources.provenance_note: Announcement; retail availability October 14. This is NOT the first-ever voice assistant, nor the first standalone Siri release.

sources.title: How do you say? — Carnegie Mellon on Jibbigo
sources.provenance_note: Fall 2009 university account of English–Spanish speech translation on iPhone. Not evidence of common use across many language pairs.

sources.title: Start a conversation with Google
sources.provenance_note: Speech conversation mode expanded to 14 languages; still described as alpha. Not equivalent to translation quality or universal adoption.

sources.title: Excerpts of the President’s address to the nation
sources.provenance_note: Describes active human fighting and plans for 30,000 additional US troops in Afghanistan in early 2010. Do not date those additional deployments to 2009.

sources.title: Automated Vehicle Safety — NHTSA
sources.provenance_note: Live guidance checked for this review. Describes limited operating areas for automated fleets and driver-attention requirements of consumer vehicles; not a historical 2009 market census.

sources.title: Cornell meets DARPA Urban Challenge
sources.provenance_note: Closed-course research challenge, not everyday automated public-highway infrastructure.

sources.title: Mortality in the United States, 2019 — CDC Data Brief 395
sources.provenance_note: Final US period life expectancy for 2019: 78.8 years. A national period measure, not a prediction of a newborn cohort’s eventual lifespan.

sources.title: Mortality in the United States, 2024 — CDC Data Brief 548
sources.provenance_note: Final US period life expectancy for 2024: 79.0 years. Do not call this a 2026 observation.

sources.title: TOP500 — November 2009 list
sources.provenance_note: Jaguar Rmax 1.759 petaflops; Rpeak 2.331 petaflops. Rmax is measured LINPACK performance, not brain emulation.

sources.title: TOP500 — November 2012 list
sources.provenance_note: Sequoia Rpeak 20.13266 petaflops and Rmax 16.32475; Titan Rpeak 27.11255 and Rmax 17.59. Peak and measured values must not be mixed.

sources.title: TOP500 — June 2013 highlights
sources.provenance_note: Tianhe-2 recorded 33.86 petaflops Rmax. This establishes a public measured milestone, not a cognition milestone.

sources.title: Large Language Models Pass the Turing Test — Jones and Bergen
sources.provenance_note: Five-minute experimental protocol. GPT-4.5 with a humanlike persona was judged human in 73% of the reported comparisons. Not the two-hour Long Bets protocol.

sources.title: ECG app and irregular rhythm notification available on Apple Watch
sources.provenance_note: AFib-related features are limited-purpose. The release expressly lists conditions they cannot detect; not general diagnosis or autonomous treatment.

sources.title: What educators need to know about cochlear implants — FDA
sources.provenance_note: Cochlear implants do not restore normal hearing. Used to correct a medical error in our intake, not to manufacture a Kurzweil forecast.

sources.title: Waymo opens more rides in Denver, San Diego and Tampa
sources.provenance_note: Driverless fleet operations exist. Regional launches do not establish elimination of most human driving or a road-controlled intelligent-highway system.

sources.title: iRobot reports third-quarter financial results
sources.provenance_note: Cumulative robot sales are not a household adoption rate; use only as capability/deployment evidence.
